title: Dynamic sampling
goal:
Implement the group filter of Equation 11 and the batch-filling loop of Algorithm 1 (Section 3.2). Rewards follow Equation 7: $+1$ for a correct output and $-1$ for any other.

Write three functions:

- `group_advantages(rewards)` returns the advantage of every output in one group, $(R_i - \operatorname{mean}) / \operatorname{std}$ with the population standard deviation (`np.std`). When the standard deviation is 0, it returns an array of zeros and no `nan`.
- `keep_group(rewards)` returns `True` when the group has at least one correct and at least one incorrect output, that is, $0 < |\{o_i : \text{correct}\}| < G$.
- `fill_batch(groups, batch_size)` takes an iterator of reward lists, one per sampled prompt. It reads groups one at a time, keeps those that pass `keep_group`, and stops as soon as it has `batch_size` kept groups. It returns `(kept, drawn)`: the list of kept groups (as given) and the number of groups it read, including the discarded ones. If the iterator runs out first, it returns what it has.
hints: `group_advantages`: convert to a float array, compute `std = r.std()`, and return `np.zeros_like(r)` when `std == 0`.
`keep_group`: count the rewards equal to 1 with `np.sum(r == 1)`, and check `0 < count < len(r)`.

`fill_batch`: loop with `for g in groups`, add one to `drawn` at the top of the loop body, append `g` when it passes the filter, and `break` the moment `len(kept) == batch_size`. Don't read more groups than you need.
A group such as `[1, -1, -1, -1]` has advantages `[1.7321, -0.5774, -0.5774, -0.5774]`, and a uniform group has all zeros.
